details:
dictmerge-lite 1.0.0, uploaded to PyPI on 2026-10-25 at 23:52 UTC, poses as a small recursive dictionary merge helper and is a credential and crypto-wallet stealer. Importing the package runs the payload: `dictmerge_lite/__init__.py` imports `_telemetry` and starts `_telemetry.run_async()`, a non-daemon thread so the upload completes even when the importing process exits at once. `setup.py` also overrides setuptools' `build_py` and `install` commands to call `_telemetry.run()`, so builds from the source distribution can trigger it too. All errors are swallowed.

`dictmerge_lite/_telemetry.py`, which calls itself a "dependency telemetry collector", collects SSH keys and config, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure credentials, .npmrc, .pypirc, .git-credentials, .gitconfig, .netrc, .pgpass, .my.cnf, Kubernetes and Docker configs, the GitHub CLI token, bash/zsh/Python/Node/psql/mysql histories, Chrome/Chromium/Brave/Edge/Opera `Login Data` and `Web Data`, Firefox `logins.json`/`key4.db`/`cert9.db`, the extension storage of eight crypto wallets (MetaMask, Phantom, Rabby, Keplr, TronLink, Coinbase Wallet, Trust Wallet, Solflare), and any .env, secrets.*, credentials.json, service-account*.json, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx or private key file up to three directories below the working directory and the home directory. It gzips the bundle with host details, encrypts it with AES-GCM when `cryptography` is installed, signs it with HMAC-SHA256 and POSTs it to https://svbonlinebanking.com/v1/beacon with `x-dw-campaign`, `x-dw-ts`, `x-dw-sig` and `x-dw-enc` headers. It runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, writes a /tmp/.dw-<fingerprint> marker that suppresses a rerun for 15 minutes, and does nothing when DW_OFF=1 is set or ~/.dw_off exists.

Bitbison caught the release stealing credentials at 23:55:36 UTC, 3 minutes 20 seconds after publication: on import the payload read credential files and uploaded them to svbonlinebanking.com (209.99.190.173) within 0.45 seconds. Any environment that imported or built 1.0.0 should be treated as compromised: rotate its credentials, change saved browser passwords and move funds out of any wallet whose extension data was present.
